newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch truckers sought Spanish govt intervention.
newsitem.headline: Dutch truckers sought Spanish govt intervention.

text.p: Three Dutch transport and shippers' organisations said they sent a joint letter to the Spanish goverment asking that the goverment intervene in the Spanish truckers' strike.
A spokesman for the organisations said the strike had so far cost the Dutch industry nearly 10 million guilders.

In a joint statement, the the Royal Netherlands Transport Association(KNV), the Dutch Transport and Logistic Association(TLN) and the EVO, the shippers' organisation, said they estimated that more than 100 Dutch truckers were now held up in Spain.
The organisation leading the strike, Fedatrans, met Spanish government representatives for a second day of negotiations on Sunday but no progress was evident.

A Spanish government official, asked by Reuters if an agreement could be reached on Sunday, was sceptical. "It's very premature. It's a long and complicated process," said the official, who asked not to be named.

"The situation in Spain is unacceptable. For instance, if foreign truckers do not follow the instructions of the Spanish drivers, their reaction is to slash tyres, smash windows or cut fuel pipes," the Dutch statement said.
The spokesman added: "It is impossible to move around in Spain even if companies manage to fly their goods into the country."
Drivers are being held at industrial parks, car parks and at petrol stations and they are guarded by Spanish truckers, the Dutch groups said.

The organisations, which represent more than 90 percent of international trucking companies in the Netherlands and the majority of Dutch shippers, said they had also written to the European transport commissioner for Transport, Neil Kinnock and the Dutch transport minister, pointing out that the Spanish government had scarcely taken action against the violent behaviour of the Spanish truck drivers.
They also pointed out in their letters that there was a European Union agreement which guarantees free movement of traffic of goods within the European market.
The three organisations said that such situations had cost the Dutch industry 130 million guilders last year.
TLN represents 7,000 transport operators responsible for 90 percent of all cross-border traffic and 70 percent of all inland haulage.
